scope: Architecture/ADRs/glossary/schema and linked contract boundaries. Read-only; no repository changes.
method: Audit ladder L0–L7, seams then invariants then planted schema failures and numeric re-derivation.

findings.title: Shipped authority writes bypass the journal projection transaction
findings.impact: Grant/effect state is neither atomically produced nor replayable. A failure after the event but before the row gives a durable claim without the represented state; the grant id is generated only after its event and cannot be recovered from that event.

evidence.note: Every state change is an event; every register is rebuildable without identity changes.
Append and synchronous projections are one transaction.
grant.issued append followed by direct grants insert, with no grant id in event.
effect append, effect_intents insert, grants update, consumed append are separate calls.
Only registers event types; no authority projector.
M137/M138/M139 marked shipped.

findings.remedy: Move grant creation, consumption and effect receipt projections behind the append transaction. Mint stable ids before append. Use an effect intent/attempt/observed-outcome state machine for the filesystem boundary; recording an effect cannot itself make filesystem writes atomic with Postgres. Reconcile crash/unknown outcomes explicitly.
findings.acceptance: Planted failures before/after each write leave one coherent state; journal-only rebuild preserves grant/effect ids and consumption; concurrent attempts cannot spend one grant twice.
findings.verification: Static direct call-chain confirmed; live concurrency probe delegated to core audit.

findings.title: Projection rebuild is not idempotent and the equality test omits the drifting fields
findings.impact: Every replay increments config_revision again; project.created does not reset status/configuration metadata. Rebuild can invent revisions or retain corruption while reporting success.

evidence.note: Latest rebuild implementation only replays all events over current tables.
project.created conflict update does not reset config_revision/status; subsequent updates increment revision.
config_revision = config_revision + 1 on each replay.
P5 compares only id/name/status/repo_path and memory id/claim.
Every projector promises rebuild() == current.

findings.remedy: Make projection application deterministic from journal identity/sequence; rebuild into a clean or correctly reset generation while preserving references, and define orphan handling. Verify all projection columns, not selected examples.
findings.acceptance: On representative data compare complete logical rowsets before/after two rebuilds; plant corrupted config_revision/status/primary repo/validity data; restore original rows and identities; no extra journal facts created.
findings.verification: Static proof and deficient P5 assertion inspected; live SQL verification requested from core.

findings.title: The canonical NodeResult facade cannot satisfy the exact contract it claims to implement
findings.impact: A runner built from the canonical module specification will produce envelopes rejected by Fabric Agent Contract. This is an implementation blocker for slice 3, not evidence that the presently unbuilt SDK runner is malfunctioning.

evidence.note: Says aligned with contract 0.1.0, then done/scope/notVerified strings and extra costUsdEstimate.
Normative external repository; exact revision; do not copy schemas.
Requires id/contractVersion/outcome/createdAt/producer in addition to four proof fields.
done is array; scope object at 40; notVerified array at 52; additionalProperties false at 69.

findings.remedy: Consume one machine-readable exact revision and derive/import result types. Either use the normative envelope directly or define and test an explicit internal-to-external translator; put local cost metadata outside the closed envelope. Synchronize the documentation in the same change.
findings.acceptance: The documented NodeResult example and a real runner result pass the pinned conformance validator; missing proof scope and extra top-level cost field fail; no copied parallel envelope survives.
findings.verification: Executed Draft202012 validation against git show 489737051828fafec92463df04b6a6fd3280c7b7: 9 violations including three wrong field types.

findings.title: Project blueprint validation accepts impossible manager and capability bindings
findings.impact: The explanatory schema suite prints a green boundary verdict for two active PMs, a retired sole PM, and a routine requesting a capability absent from its selected provider binding. Future consumers cannot rely on the advertised project-boundary fixture coverage.

evidence.note: Only checks selected manager id resolves, not total active PM count/status.
Only checks preferred agent exists, not whether it can serve capability.
Generic agentBinding array does not enforce manager cardinality.
PW-REQ-002 claims manager-resolution verification.

findings.remedy: Add semantic project validation for exactly one enabled manager and valid routine/binding capability relation, including disabled/retired eligibility. Name fallback policy explicitly if capability selection may legitimately change.
findings.acceptance: All three isolated mutated examples below fail; current examples pass. Add negative fixtures for duplicate PM, retired PM, unknown/unbound capability and disabled routine selection, without duplicating the normative provider schema.
findings.verification: Executed checker in temporary copy for each planted mutation: each returned exit 0 and OK: 3 schemas and 4 examples are valid; 4 invalid boundary probes were rejected.

findings.title: The implemented MCP session profile and the canonical protocol pin describe different protocols
findings.impact: The local server depends on initialize and mcp-session-id, while all current architecture points to stateless MCP 2026-07-28. A client following the canonical pin is refused as uninitialized. Blind SDK upgrading would also invalidate the security rationale of the one-use credential handshake.

evidence.note: Protocol pin MCP 2026-07-28.
server/discover replaces initialize and per-request metadata is the declared doctrine.
Stateful StreamableHTTP transport; session id generated.
Requests without initialized session refused.
M15 labels the locally served half southbound, despite its Fabric-server direction.

findings.remedy: Record a supported-protocol matrix separating the current loopback session profile from the planned northbound 2026 profile. State the compatibility and auth transition explicitly. If upgrading, redesign the credential binding for stateless requests before replacing the handshake.
findings.acceptance: Contract tests cover one supported legacy client and one 2026 client or give the latter an explicit unsupported-version outcome; docs and SDK-supported version set match; replay/revocation/credential-scope fixtures survive the transition.
findings.verification: Installed SDK exports latest 2025-11-25 and supports no 2026 revision. Official 2026 specification and Tasks overview fetched 2026-09-05 confirm stateless/per-request capabilities.

findings.impact: Readers cannot determine what exists, and obsolete open decisions can be reopened while unfinished clauses marked shipped disappear from the plan.

32 ADRs vs measured 33.
Verification ledger called empty despite populated rows.
Says no server implemented.

findings.remedy: Update entry-point current-state paragraphs and resolve superseded CO rows by referencing their deciding ADRs. Split partial milestone acceptance from the original scope; preserve unfinished tiered-fact work as a counted extension of M48. Generate counts from canonical registries and add a small status drift gate for mechanical claims.

findings.verification: Re-derived via filesystem: 33 ADRs, 12 architecture markdown files, 15 migrations; verification rows present. Status contradictions verified at cited lines.

findings.title: Task has three meanings and no accepted mapping to the future work lifecycle
findings.impact: The current PTY request is promised to become a Run with the same id; the planned board task instead persists through planning, sessions and work history. Implementing board and runner separately risks assigning incompatible lifecycle/cardinality semantics to one id.

evidence.note: Task on its own is explicitly forbidden; no Task definition.
Task = instruction plus session; promises to become a Run retaining identity.
Run is one graph execution; terminal state immutable.
M54 task detail owns multiple sessions and commits.
M122 board becomes canonical task state.
M143 task has brief, append-only notes, transitions and effects.

findings.remedy: Decide and document the work-item, execution Run, graph Node, terminal Session, and MCP Task mapping before new schema or screen work. Name cardinalities and state transitions; specify migration of existing project_tasks ids and receipt links. A task-to-many-runs model is a candidate, not a silently adopted decision.
findings.acceptance: One planned task can undergo the accepted retry/continuation flow without mutating a terminal Run or losing old session/transcript history; all screen states and APIs trace to the same enum and entity definition.
findings.verification: Cross-document contradiction directly observed; no choice made during this read-only audit.

findings.title: Withdrawal of the old external provider was applied to one section but not its dependent architecture
findings.impact: The foundry bootstrap still requires a product explicitly removed from this estate on 2026-09-03; active sections still assert code ownership and integration with it. Following the plan would reintroduce the withdrawn dependency.

evidence.note: Operator removed a side project from estate scope 2026-09-03.
Still says Fabric consumes that provider.
Still says we own its code.
Still first measured external provider.
Still bootstrap product #4.
Still claims the example is current.

findings.remedy: Propagate withdrawal through active dependency/bootstrapping sections and scope notes, retaining historical measurements as explicitly historical. Choose a current authorized sample provider when the foreign-provider milestone opens; do not silently substitute another product.
findings.acceptance: Scope search returns the withdrawn name only in dated historical evidence or explicit exclusions; M37 bootstrap has a runnable named current consumer/provider or an explicit prerequisite.
findings.verification: Scope-change and remaining instructions read directly; historical registry measurements are not treated as bugs by themselves.

findings.title: Transcript decoding changes what was displayed while the raw evidence is discarded
findings.impact: The primary session memory can contain text never displayed (backspace/cursor writes) or omit text that remained visible. A checksum of the transformed text does not restore the source that was deleted.

evidence.note: Primary durable memory is whole verbatim transcript.
Claims deterministic transport decode identical to what operator saw; raw not retained.
Regex strips cursor movement and backspace; last CR segment replaces full line.
Tests equal-length progress repaint only.

findings.remedy: Preserve primary input/output evidence with explicit capture semantics; use a real terminal-state decoder for display-derived text or a structured runner transcript. Keep searchable decoded text as a derived projection, mark truncation/loss modes, and version decoder semantics. Decide retention of raw bytes without silently claiming full losslessness.
findings.acceptance: Fixture abc\rXY renders XYc; abc\bX renders abX; abc\x1b[2DX renders aXc; actual terminal repaint traces retain the required source. Tests fail when control handling is replaced with stripping; prior capture limitations remain visible.
findings.verification: Executed direct imports of production decodePty: inputs yielded XY, abcX, abcX respectively. Source preservation and decoder mismatch are proven; impact on real captured Claude UI traces not quantified.

findings.title: The detailed module design is not an as-built map for the components already shipped
findings.impact: Memory is described as content-addressed Storage but persists full body in both journal JSON and a SQL text projection. The promised signature-compatible policy port instead has allow/refuse, no returned receiptSeq, and no autonomy/accessCeiling inputs. These are material integration and capacity differences, not reasons to implement the entire future architecture now.

evidence.note: Says transcripts whole/content-addressed in Storage.
Session transcript Storage row.
Appends full transcript body into journal payload.
Projects full transcript body into session_transcripts.
Promises signature-compatible decide with allow/deny/indeterminate and receiptSeq.
Actual EffectRequest has caller-supplied floorClass; Decision is allow/refuse without receipt identity.

findings.remedy: Add explicit as-built/diet mapping to canonical module sections with current code homes and APIs, and keep future ports separately versioned. Either adapt Policy to the promised port now or remove the compatibility claim and record its bounded migration task. Document current SQL transcript storage and its backup/retention implications; Storage adoption needs the existing artifact-store gate.
findings.acceptance: An API fixture compiles against declared policy signature and checks receipt identity and indeterminate behavior; inventory states exactly which data is SQL versus blob Storage and proves journal→projection relation; no directory/package diagram implies packages that do not exist.
findings.verification: Only packages/schema and packages/journal exist. Policy/memory/runner are currently app-main modules; direct code and migration read verified data path.

strengths: The project deliberately distinguishes Product/Kernel, Estate/Project/Goal/Run and claim/observation, and records major reversals append-only.
Org1-first sequence and named return triggers keep future federation/marketplace/Temporal from becoming present implementation requirements.
Journal ordering/closed type set/lock retry, project memory boundaries, per-session MCP scoping and primary-repo derivation have concrete code and named tests.
No reason found to reverse Postgres/Electron/capability binding/durable-port choices wholesale; defects are in enforcement and integration, not proof that another stack is required.
blindspots: Core/security agent owns live SQL/permission/race and full test execution; ARCH-01/02 need their live evidence merged.
UX agent owns all screen/mockup/screenshot/a11y checks; ADR24 assessment here is architectural only.
Full historic vendor quotas, licensing, price measurements and scientific memory benchmarks were not independently reproduced. Claude SDK source URL fetch failed due tool content-length limit.
No provider admission runtime or cross-estate hosted deployment exists to execute those future-path guarantees. Their absence is recorded as planned scope, not a failing runtime.
No real transcript corpus loss-rate or storage growth benchmark measured; decoder counterexamples are exact but prevalence is unknown.
Linked contract and adapter reviewed for pin/schema/interface relation, not full standalone repository/security audits.
Dated derived HTML snapshots explicitly marked historical were not treated as current architecture claims.
